pr.title: Toggle assert_unsafe_precondition in codegen instead of expansion
pr.description:
The goal of this PR is to make some of the unsafe precondition checks in the standard library available in debug builds. Some UI tests are included to verify that it does that.

The diff is large, but most of it is blessing mir-opt tests and I've also split up this PR so it can be reviewed commit-by-commit.

This PR:
1. Adds a new intrinsic, `debug_assertions` which is lowered to a new MIR NullOp, and only to a constant after monomorphization
2. Rewrites `assume_unsafe_precondition` to check the new intrinsic, and be monomorphic.
3. Skips codegen of the `assume` intrinsic in unoptimized builds, because that was silly before but with these checks it's *very* silly
4. The checks with the most overhead are `ptr::read`/`ptr::write` and `NonNull::new_unchecked`. I've simply added `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` to the checks for `ptr::read`/`ptr::write` because I was unable to come up with any (good) ideas for decreasing their impact. But for `NonNull::new_unchecked` I found that the majority of callers can use a different function, often a safe one.

Yes, this PR slows down the compile time of some programs. But in our benchmark suite it's never more than 1% icount, and the average icount change in debug-full programs is 0.22%. I think that is acceptable for such an improvement in developer experience.

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/120539#issuecomment-1922687101
pr.author: saethlin

analysis.summary: The PR moves the `cfg!(debug_assertions)` decision for `assert_unsafe_precondition!` from macro-expansion time to a new MIR `NullOp::DebugAssertions`: `LowerIntrinsics` lowers the new `debug_assertions()` intrinsic to that NullOp, `ConstPropLint` and `GVN` deliberately refuse to fold it before monomorphization, and codegen materializes `sess.opts.debug_assertions` as a bool. The same PR also teaches `InstSimplify` to mark calls to `#[rustc_nounwind]` functions as `UnwindAction::Unreachable`, admits the new NullOp in `PromoteTemps`, and adjusts `Inline` tests because the new `#[inline(never)]` precondition-check functions change inlining.
analysis.trigger: Build core/std with debug assertions disabled while a downstream crate is compiled with `-Cdebug-assertions=yes`, or compile optimized code containing unsafe-precondition checks for APIs such as `slice::from_raw_parts`, `hint::assert_unchecked`, `NonNull::new_unchecked`, or `ptr::copy`. The `InstSimplify` part triggers on any MIR `Call` to a `#[rustc_nounwind]` function, closure, or coroutine whose ABI cannot unwind.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `assert_unsafe_precondition!` expanded to `if cfg!(debug_assertions) { ... const_eval_select(... runtime ...) }`, where the runtime checks were generic helpers such as `fn runtime$(<$($tt)*>)?($($i:$ty),*)`. Consequently the debug-assertion condition was resolved while expanding the defining crate (std/core), not while monomorphizing the caller; a std built without debug assertions omitted these checks in all downstream monomorphizations. `Option::unwrap_unchecked` also carried a separate `debug_assert!(self.is_some());`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation is to resolve the debug-assertion condition too early: evaluate `cfg!(debug_assertions)` during macro expansion, or const-fold/fold the new `debug_assertions` intrinsic or `NullOp::DebugAssertions` during MIR const-prop before monomorphization. Doing so bakes in the defining library's debug-assertion setting and can delete checks that the monomorphizing caller requested; using a generic runtime check helper also duplicates the check in every monomorphization. The replacement transformation is: `LowerIntrinsics` rewrites `debug_assertions()` into an assignment of `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::DebugAssertions, bool)` followed by a `Goto`; `ConstPropLint` and `GVN` return `None` for that NullOp; codegen reads `sess.opts.debug_assertions`; and the runtime pre-check is monomorphic, `#[inline(never)]`, and `#[rustc_nounwind]`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs that call core APIs guarded by `assert_unsafe_precondition!` (for example `slice::from_raw_parts`, `hint::assert_unchecked`, `NonNull::new_unchecked`, `ptr::copy`, `ptr::read`/`ptr::write`, and `char::from_u32_unchecked`), compiled with combinations of `-Cdebug-assertions=yes/no`, `-Copt-level`, and panic abort/unwind. For the `InstSimplify` rule, the input domain is MIR bodies containing calls to nounwind functions, closures (`Abi::RustCall`), or coroutines (`Abi::Rust`).
preconditions: LowerIntrinsics only rewrites a call to `sym::debug_assertions` when a target block is present; it pushes an assignment of `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::DebugAssertions, tcx.types.bool)` to the destination and then turns the terminator into `Goto { target }`.

The new intrinsic must be registered as safe and typed as taking no arguments and returning `bool`; the patch adds `sym::debug_assertions` to the `hir::Unsafety::Normal` list and `(0, Vec::new(), tcx.types.bool)` to intrinsic type checking.
Every MIR producer/consumer must handle the new NullOp: typeck, borrowck, validation, const checking, move-path building, pretty-printing, StableMIR, clippy const-fn qualification, and codegen.

ConstPropLint and GVN must return `None` for `NullOp::DebugAssertions`; the value is not a compile-time constant until after monomorphization and must be emitted from `sess.opts.debug_assertions` at codegen.
The interpreter deliberately evaluates `NullOp::DebugAssertions` to `false`, because the interpreter performs the relevant checks itself.
PromoteTemps' `Validator` accepts `NullOp::DebugAssertions` in its rvalue match, so the new NullOp does not make an otherwise valid candidate unpromotable.

InstSimplify's nounwind rule requires `func.const_fn_def()`, computes the body ABI as `FnDef` -> `fn_sig(...).abi()`, `Closure` -> `Abi::RustCall`, `Coroutine` -> `Abi::Rust`, and only then sets `UnwindAction::Unreachable` when `layout::fn_can_unwind(...)` is false.
pitfalls: Do not fold `NullOp::DebugAssertions` in ConstPropLint or GVN before monomorphization: the folded value would reflect the defining crate's debug-assertion setting, not the caller's.
Do not guard the unsafe-precondition check with expansion-time `cfg!(debug_assertions)`; the guard must survive into MIR and be resolved at codegen/monomorphization.

Do not make the runtime `precondition_check` generic; it is intentionally monomorphic, `#[inline(never)]`, and `#[rustc_nounwind]` to avoid code-size duplication and to allow the nounwind optimization.
The interpreter must not execute the runtime check; it returns `false` for `NullOp::DebugAssertions` because it already knows the runtime state better.
In InstSimplify, do not mark the unwind edge unreachable for a call that may unwind; closure and coroutine ABIs must be classified correctly, and the call itself must remain.
Because `assume` codegen is skipped for `OptLevel::No` and `OptLevel::Less`, tests expecting an emitted `assume` or an optimized `assume` must pin optimization/debug-assertion flags.

MIR tests are sensitive to debug assertions and panic strategy: the new checks add `cfg!(debug_assertions)` branches and `precondition_check` calls, so tests may need `-Cdebug-assertions=no` or `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`.
analysis.testStrategy: Use mir-opt `EMIT_MIR` diffs to inspect `DataflowConstProp` and `GVN` on `default_boxed_slice`: the expected MIR keeps `_8 = cfg!(debug_assertions); switchInt(move _8) -> ...` and a `precondition_check` call rather than replacing the NullOp with a constant. For `Inline`, compile `unwrap_unchecked` with `-Zmir-opt-level=2 -Zinline-mir -Cdebug-assertions=no` so the new `#[inline(never)]` precondition check does not suppress the inlining under test. Add UI `run-fail` tests compiled with `-Copt-level=3 -Cdebug-assertions=yes` and match messages such as `unsafe precondition(s) violated: slice::from_raw_parts` for misaligned/null slices and `unsafe precondition(s) violated: hint::assert_unchecked` for out-of-bounds `get_unchecked`. For assembly/codegen tests, use optimized builds with `-Cdebug-assertions=no` (the patch changes `is_aligned` to `-Copt-level=2 -Cdebug-assertions=no` and `-Copt-level=s -Cdebug-assertions=no`) to verify the checks disappear. No compiler was built or executed in this analysis; these are test directives visible in the patch.
evidence: Adds a new intrinsic, `debug_assertions` which is lowered to a new MIR NullOp, and only to a constant after monomorphization
Skips codegen of the `assume` intrinsic in unoptimized builds
// The checks hidden behind this are always better done by the interpreter
